title: 2026-10-22_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_784
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy Fysbis Linux backdoor compromise in the target network.
outcomes: Investigation of suspicious services and processes

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using their Fysbis Linux backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any connected hosts. Enter `start` to begin.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any connected hosts. Enter `start` to begin.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: While monitoring the target host, you noticed unusual network activity. Investigate the target host to identify any suspicious services or processes that might be responsible for this activity.
levels.solution: Check running services and processes using commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service`, `ps aux`, or `top`. Look for any unusual or unexpected services or processes. The suspicious service is named `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and processes, looking for anything unusual or unexpected.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service`, `ps aux`, or `top` to investigate services and processes.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Try using `systemctl status bkd.service` to get more information about the suspicious service.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: You've identified a suspicious service running on the target host. Determine how this service is automatically started after a system reboot.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd services, cron jobs, or other persistence mechanisms. The persistence mechanism is a systemd service named `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services, cron jobs, or other persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Try using `systemctl cat bkd.service` to inspect the service configuration.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: You suspect that the attacker might be moving laterally from the target host to other systems in the network. Investigate any evidence of file transfers or remote execution that could indicate lateral movement.
levels.solution: Check for any scripts or services that transfer files or execute commands on other hosts. The service used for lateral movement is named `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check for any scripts or services that transfer files or execute commands on other hosts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `ps aux`, `systemctl list-units --type=service`, or `ls /usr/local/bin/`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Try using `systemctl status payload-transfer.service` to get more information about the service.
